sentences.cn_text: 终有一日，《纽约时报》将停止在新闻纸上刊登报道。
sentences.en_text: There will eventually come a day when The New York Times ceases to publish stories on newsprint.

sentences.cn_text: 具体日期尚无定论。该报出版商在2010年曾表示：「在未来某个时候」。
sentences.en_text: Exactly when that day will be is a matter of debate. “Sometime in the future,” the paper’s publisher said back in 2010.

sentences.cn_text: 抛开对纸墨油香和翻页沙响的怀旧情结，放弃印刷版确有诸多理由。
sentences.en_text: Nostalgia for ink on paper and the rustle of pages aside, there’s plenty of incentive to ditch print.

sentences.cn_text: 制作实体报纸所需的基础设施——印刷机、配送车辆——不仅成本高昂，在纯线上竞争对手无此财务负担的时代更显得过度冗余。
sentences.en_text: The infrastructure required to make a physical newspaper — printing presses, delivery trucks — isn’t just expensive; it’s excessive at a time when online-only competitors don’t have the same set of financial constraints.

sentences.cn_text: 读者本就在逐步远离印刷媒体。
sentences.en_text: Readers are migrating away from print anyway.

sentences.cn_text: 虽然印刷广告销售额仍远超线上和移动端，但印刷收入持续下滑。
sentences.en_text: And though print ad sales still dwarf their online and mobile counterparts, revenue from print is still declining.

sentences.cn_text: BuzzFeed首席执行官乔纳·佩雷蒂表示，尽管成本居高不下、发行量日渐萎缩，但贸然取消印刷版将铸成大错。
sentences.en_text: Overhead may be high and circulation lower, but rushing to eliminate its print edition would be a mistake, says BuzzFeed CEO Jonah Peretti.

sentences.cn_text: 佩雷蒂认为《纽约时报》不应在退出印刷业务上浪费时间，但前提是方法得当。他说：「找到加速这一转型的办法对他们而言是明智之举，但如果直接停刊，会让最忠实的客户极度不满。」
sentences.en_text: Peretti says the Times shouldn’t waste time getting out of the print business, but only if they go about doing it the right way. “Figuring out a way to accelerate that transition would make sense for them,” he said, “but if you discontinue it, you’re going to have your most loyal customers really upset with you.”

sentences.cn_text: 有时这种代价仍值得为变革付出。
sentences.en_text: Sometimes that’s worth making a change anyway.

sentences.cn_text: 佩雷蒂举例说Netflix停止DVD邮寄服务转向流媒体，「当时被视为失策」，他说。
sentences.en_text: Peretti gives the example of Netflix discontinuing its DVD-mailing service to focus on streaming. “It was seen as a blunder,” he said.

sentences.cn_text: 事后证明此举颇具远见。
sentences.en_text: The move turned out to be foresighted.

sentences.cn_text: 若由佩雷蒂执掌《纽约时报》？「我不会设定停印年限」，他说，「我会提价，将其打造成更具传承价值的产品。」
sentences.en_text: And if Peretti were in charge at the Times? “I wouldn’t pick a year to end print,” he said. “I would raise prices and make it into more of a legacy product.”

sentences.cn_text: 按此思路，最忠实的客户仍能获得心仪的产品,并感到自己在维护所信奉事物的品质。「若你为印刷版多付费，会觉得是在提供帮助」，佩雷蒂说，「然后每年以更高幅度提价，实质上尝试创造额外收入。」
sentences.en_text: The most loyal customers would still get the product they favor, the idea goes, and they’d feel like they were helping sustain the quality of something they believe in. “So if you’re overpaying for print, you could feel like you were helping,” Peretti said. “Then increase it at a higher rate each year and essentially try to generate additional revenue.”

sentences.cn_text: 换言之,若要制作印刷产品，就应面向那些对其痴迷的人群。
sentences.en_text: In other words, if you’re going to make a print product, make it for the people who are already obsessed with it.

sentences.cn_text: 这或许正是《纽约时报》的现行策略。
sentences.en_text: Which may be what the Times is doing already.

sentences.cn_text: 全周七天订阅印刷版年费近500美元——是纯数字订阅的两倍有余。
sentences.en_text: Getting the print edition seven days a week costs nearly $500 a year — more than twice as much as a digital-only subscription.

sentences.cn_text: 「这是极其艰难的抉择，BuzzFeed没有传统业务包袱是巨大优势」，佩雷蒂评论道，「但我们也会面临类似问题，即当市场和世界变化时，我们所做之事可能不再合理。」
sentences.en_text: “It’s a really hard thing to do and it’s a tremendous luxury that BuzzFeed doesn’t have a legacy business,” Peretti remarked. “But we’re going to have questions like that where we have things we’re doing that don’t make sense when the market changes and the world changes.

sentences.cn_text: 在此类情形下，宁可激进，不可保守。
sentences.en_text: In those situations, it’s better to be more aggressive than less aggressive.”
